contract.sync_assumed: none beyond warp convergence of the logical warp's lanes
contract.type_constraints: bf16 keys packed into one 32-bit word (key bits high, inverted 16-bit index low, N at most 65536), fp32 keys packed into one 64-bit word (key bits high, inverted 32-bit index low), int32 source indices derived from the striped position
contract.nan_behavior: a NaN key orders by its sign bit (positive NaN above every finite key, negative NaN below), deterministic, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is mapped to +0.0 before packing so the two zeros compare equal
contract.tie_break_support: inherent in the word order: among equal keys the smaller index gives the larger word, prefer_smaller_index costs nothing (psi cells equal the ng cells to the cycle, same code)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted by (key descending, index ascending)
contract.k_range: [1, MaxK] with MaxK = round_up(k, 32), N / MaxK a power of two, k 4 to 16 pay the k 32 network
contract.n_range: N = 32 x IPT with IPT a power of two, measured 64, 128 and 256 (bf16 N at most 65536)

correctness.notes: Oracle battery passed in every cell for both requirements (exact prefer_smaller_index check included). Control W1_packed in the same lock section for both requirements (it supports both). This is the N2 kill experiment (idea card ideas/queue/N2_level_parallel_bitonic.md, explore item 1) extended to N 128 and 256: variant and control share the packed words, so only the stage order and the compare-exchange codegen differ. Built on the node against the shared harness at swarm commit b6bfae9a37bb, sources at W1 worktree commit 851d41cc5c. The first measurement of this variant (batch W1_level_vs_W1_packed_focus_kill_n2_20261025_131737.json, code at commit ccc1166d9c) had the word array in local memory at N 256 (T36) and is superseded by this card, its N 64 and 128 cells agree with this card to the cycle. The shuffle ablation W1_level_n64 (whole-word 64-bit shuffle intrinsic) measured 1.00x against W1_level in every cell in the same session (batch W1_level_vs_W1_level_n64_focus_fix3_20261025_134401.json), the CUDA 13.4 header already splits the 64-bit shuffle. Two W1 optimizer instances shared one agent id on 2026-10-25. This card is Instance A (opt-W1, worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1, branch exp/topk-swarm/W1): the N2 verdict here is W1_level against W1_packed (the CUB eager network on the same packed words). Instance B (opt-W1b) owns the same-code eager against level comparison with min max stages and the fp32 native min max pairs variant (cards W1_eager_same, W1_level_pairs, W1_minmax_pairs on B200), report approaches/W1/REPORT_W1b.md.

low_level: Stage codegen: the exchange written as keep_max ? max(k, other) : min(k, other) compiles to two predicated VIMNMX.U32 per shuffle stage for the bf16 u32 words (71 VIMNMX for 35 stages plus one pairing max at N 64, 5 SEL in the whole network) against ISETP, ISETP, PLOP3, SEL in the CUB comparator path of the control (172 ISETP, 76 SEL, 2 VIMNMX at N 64). Same shuffle count (35 per network at N 64), 196 against 212 SASS instructions per network. For the fp32 u64 words the exchange is ISETP.LE.U32 then ISETP.LE.U32.XOR.EX (the keep_max predicate folded into the .EX compare) then two SEL, the control's is two independent ISETP pairs, a PLOP3 and two predicated SEL, 300 against 304 instructions per network: the u64 instruction mix is the same in both, only the stage order differs.

Registers of the latency kernel: bf16 35 at N 64, 40 to 41 at N 128, 56 at N 256 (control 23 to 24, 27, 31 to 32), fp32 37, 43 to 44 (56 at k 64), 61 to 64 (control 28 to 29, 30 to 40, 32 to 48). Throughput kernel bf16 23 to 32, fp32 28 to 48, occupancy 8 blocks of 256 per SM except fp32 N 128 k 64 (6) and N 256 k 64 (5). No spills, no stack frame, BRA count equals the no-op kernel's (5), no branch inside the network (T20).

The first version of this network put the word array in local memory in the latency kernel (80 bytes stack frame, 0 spill bytes, STL 11 and LDL 11 at fp32 N 256 k 64) while the throughput kernel of the same TU kept it in registers, and measured 14871 cycles instead of 3565 with the same instruction stream. Cause: the array was indexed through pointer offsets inside cuda::static_for lambdas and #pragma unroll loops, and in the kernel that inlines the network twice the alloca escaped. Template recursion with every index a compile-time constant fixed every cell (T36, with T34 for the unroll threshold).

Throughput reading with T33: at N 128 bf16 the level network issues 35 plus 2 times 6 shuffle stages for 4 words per lane against the control's 15 plus 3 times 20, the same 75 shuffles per lane and 8 warps per block, so the 1.40x throughput gain (370 against 264 Gelem/s) is the ALU side: 2 VIMNMX per exchange against 4 instructions, the SHFL pipe is not the limit at these sizes (4 cycles per SHFL per scheduler would allow about 2 Telem/s).
algorithmic: Kill experiment of idea card N2 at the stated cell warp N 64 k 32 (two tiles): bf16 1.30x (695 against 905 cycles, the 1.3x threshold met exactly), fp32 0.83x (1194 against 990, missed). With two tiles the eager form's two independent 15-stage sorts already overlap in ptxas's schedule, and the level form adds nothing but a different stage order, so at two tiles the result is the codegen difference (bf16 gains the VIMNMX exchange, fp32 u64 has the same instructions and loses on the schedule).

From four tiles on the restructuring pays: bf16 N 128 1.55x to 1.74x (883 against 1367 at k 16, 883 against 1521 at k 32, 916 against 1598 at k 64), N 256 2.49x to 2.55x (1115 against 2841, 1419 against 3539), fp32 N 128 2.13x to 2.29x at k 16 and 32 (1131 and 1053 against 2408), 1.55x at k 64 (1671 against 2583), N 256 2.65x and 2.56x at k 16 and 32 (1728 and 1790 against 4585), 1.48x at k 64 (3571 against 5291). Throughput 1.30x to 1.47x bf16 and 1.12x to 1.37x fp32. The cost model held in shape: 25 dependent stages at N 128 against the eager's 75, and the per-stage cost at IPT 8 is barely above IPT 4 (N 256 k 32 bf16 1115 against N 128 883 for 15 more stage-slots at IPT 8 plus a 6-stage level, about 15 cycles per added stage-slot), far below the July s(8) placeholder of 152.

Against the pairs reference W1_reference, chained through W1_packed (measured to the cycle in both sections of the same session): bf16 N 64 k 32 695 against 1164 (1.67x), N 128 k 16 883 against 2267 (2.57x), k 64 916 against 2562 (2.80x), fp32 N 128 k 16 1131 against 2038 (1.80x), k 64 1671 against 2255 (1.35x), fp32 N 64 1190 against 846 (0.71x). The level network with u64 words beats the pairs reference at fp32 from four tiles on despite the u64 overhead that costs the eager form 15 to 19 percent.

k below MaxK is free as in the eager form (k 16 and 32 share 883 at N 128 bf16), k 64 (MaxK 64, M 2) costs 4 percent more at bf16 N 128 (916) and 58 percent more at fp32 (1671): the register-register stages of the 2-word tile are cheap for u32 (two VIMNMX) and dear for u64 (two ISETP and four SEL).
prefer_smaller_index is free (psi equals ng to the cycle in every cell, same code, the word order carries the tie-break). Output sorted descending by (key, index) in the first k striped positions.
negative: fp32 at two tiles (N 64, MaxK 32): 0.83x against the eager form with the same instruction mix. The eager keeps N at most 2 MaxK for fp32, the level form takes over at N at least 4 MaxK. The gap is a schedule effect of the kind T28 describes (300 instructions per network, equal histograms, different order), not an algorithmic one.

A shuffle policy that splits the 64-bit word into two 32-bit shuffles by hand gained nothing (1.00x in every cell against the whole-word intrinsic, W1_level_n64): the CUDA 13.4 header already does exactly that without asm volatile, the hypothesis that the intrinsic pins the shuffle order was wrong.

The sub-tile idea of the N2 card (tiles narrower than the logical warp for k below 32, explore item 2) does not pay on the measured stage costs: at warp N 128 k 16 with 16-lane tiles the 5 sort stages saved per word (10 instead of 15 at IPT 4) are given back by the extra in-slot level (one shuffle max plus 4 merge stages), model 880 against the measured 883, and at k 8 with 8-lane tiles the two in-slot levels cost what the 9 saved stages save. Not built.
surprises: The eager control's latency at fixed MaxK depends on k through the output store predicate alone: bf16 N 64 1150 cycles at k 16 against 905 at k 32 (the level network's 695 is 1.65x or 1.30x depending on which), N 128 1367 against 1521, fp32 unchanged. This is T28's schedule fragility, here on the CUB comparator network with the u32 words (T28 reports the min max network free of it, which matches this card: the level network measures 883 at k 16 and 32 alike, 695 at N 64 for both k). The verdict above uses the k 32 control, the conservative one.

Phase 1 at IPT 8 costs almost the same per stage as at IPT 4 (the N 256 cells are 2.5x the eager at the same N), the July stage cost table (s(8) 152 against s(4) 70) overstates the issue cost of independent shuffles by about 5x at these sizes, consistent with T17's 5 cycles per further shuffle in flight.

The level network's u64 path is 1.55x faster than the eager at fp32 N 128 k 64 but only 1.48x at N 256 k 64 and its throughput gain shrinks to 1.12x to 1.14x there: at MaxK 64 the two-word tile makes 14 of the 21 sort stages and 2 of the 6 merge stages register stages, which for u64 are the expensive compare-and-four-selects form.
open_questions: Where exactly does the fp32 two-tile schedule lose 200 cycles against the eager with the same instruction mix, and does a dummy dependence or a different tile order (T28's perturbations) recover it? Not pursued, the two-tile case is the eager's.
Would a bf16x2 two-row variant (N5) halve the VIMNMX and SHFL count of this network in the throughput regime, where it is ALU bound at 8 blocks per SM? The index would have to leave the word.

Does the fp32 result improve with keys only (one 32-bit shuffle and one FMNMX per stage) plus an index recovery pass by ballot rank after the network (threshold from the k-th position, rank among equals in position order, which gives prefer_smaller_index as well)? Model at N 128: network about the bf16 cost (883) plus 4 registers times two ballots and popc, about 200 cycles, against 1131 now.
How does the level network compare with W2 at N 64 to 256 and k 16 to 64 in the same session? PRIORITIES.md expects W2 to own k at most 32 there, these cells are the ones to run together.

verification.notes: verify-W1 rerun 2026-10-25 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99 (GB200, nvcc 13.4.92, sm_100, the card's node), W1_level and the control W1_packed rebuilt from worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1 commit beb03e2bed (warp_level_topk.cuh, w1_common.cuh and w1_adapters.cuh byte identical to the card's 851d41cc5c) on the shared harness (topk_harness.cuh identical to b6bfae9a37bb), CCCL clone b6bfae9a37bb, same grid (--n 64,128,256 --k 16,32,64, both requirements, W1_packed as the control for both in one lock section), batch state/results/verify-W1/W1_level_vs_W1_packed_focus_v_level_20261025_141707.json. All 64 cells reproduce: latency identical to the cycle for variant and control in every cell (rerun vs card: bf16 N64 k32 695 vs 695 against W1_packed 905 vs 905, bf16 N128 k16 883 vs 883 against 1367 vs 1367, bf16 N256 k32 1115 vs 1115 against 2840 vs 2840, fp32 N64 k32 1194 vs 1194 against 990 vs 990, fp32 N128 k16 1131 vs 1131 against 2408 vs 2408, fp32 N256 k16 1728 vs 1728 against 4585 vs 4585, fp32 N256 k64 3571 vs 3571 against 5291 vs 5291), throughput within 0.14 percent (bf16 N128 k16 369.8 vs 369.7 against 263.4 vs 263.7 Gelem/s, bf16 N256 k64 270.8 vs 270.8 against 227.2 vs 227.2, fp32 N128 k64 152.1 vs 152.2 against 135.6 vs 135.4), registers, occupancy and SASS sizes identical in every cell. The kill experiment reads the same: at the stated cell N64 k32 bf16 905/695 = 1.30x (threshold met exactly), fp32 0.83x (missed); from four tiles on 1.55x to 2.55x bf16 and 1.48x to 2.65x fp32, as the card says; by the letter of the idea card (1.3x at N64 k32, key type unspecified) the stated cell is a pass for bf16 only, the survive verdict rests on the N128 and N256 cells, which the card discloses. The chain against the pairs reference holds in my own session: W1_packed measured to the cycle in the level batch and in the W1_packed rerun batch (drift 0.00 percent latency, at most 0.12 percent throughput), so level over W1_reference is bf16 N64 k32 1.67x, N128 k16 2.57x, N128 k64 2.80x, fp32 N128 k16 1.80x, N128 k64 1.35x, N64 k16 0.71x, the card's numbers. psi equals ng within 0.13 percent. Canaries 32.00098 at both ends, thr_us 3611.2/3609.8 (card 3611.1/3611.3). Oracle 13 cases per side in every cell, selftest true except the harness's vacuous k = N/2 cases (N64 k32, N128 k64, see the W1_packed card note). Anti-DCE: slope_raw at least 15.5x the no-op slope (48), r2_raw 1.0000, chain minima monotone, no STL, LDL, stack frame or BAR.SYNC in any kernel; the rebuilt fp32 N256 k64 latency kernel has 2800 instructions and no local memory (the T36 fix is in the committed source). SASS of the rebuilt kernels confirms the stage codegen claims: bf16 N64 k32 latency kernel 392 instructions with 142 VIMNMX, 5 SEL and 70 SHFL (two copies) against the control's 440 with 2 VIMNMX, 172 ISETP, 76 SEL and 70 SHFL; bf16 N128 k16 632 with 306 VIMNMX and 150 SHFL against 792 with 6 VIMNMX, 347 ISETP, 150 SHFL. Findings inaccuracies that do not change the verdict: low_level[0] says 196 against 212 instructions per network at bf16 N64 (the control kernel is 440, i.e. 220 per copy) and 300 against 304 at fp32 N64 with 'the same instruction mix'; the rebuilt fp32 N64 k32 kernels are 600 against 696 (300 against 348 per copy) and the eager control carries 264 ISETP and 20 PLOP3 against the level network's 170 ISETP and no PLOP3, so the eager has about 16 percent more instructions, not the same mix, which weakens the 'schedule, not instruction count' reading of the fp32 two-tile loss. low_level[1] quotes control latency registers of 23 to 24, 27, 31 to 32 (bf16) and 28 to 29, 30 to 40, 32 to 48 (fp32); the batch has 23 to 24, 27 to 31, 35 to 43 and 32, 41 to 42, 58 to 61. algorithmic[1] gives the bf16 throughput gain as 1.30x to 1.47x, the N256 k64 cell is 1.19x (270.8 against 227.2).
